title: Java MCQs - Part 1: Fundamentals
description: Warm up with Java basics: primitive types, operators, strings, OOP, access modifiers, exceptions and core collections.

questions.q: Which Java primitive type is a 64-bit signed integer?
What is the default value of an int instance field that is never explicitly initialized?
options: It causes a compile error when read

questions.q: Which keyword prevents a class from being subclassed?
A field or method of a class is declared with no access modifier. Where is it accessible?
options: Only from within the same class
Only from classes in the same package
From the same package and from subclasses in any package

questions.q: Which of these is a checked exception?

What is the output?

System.out.println(10 / 3 + " " + 10 % 3 + " " + 10 / 3.0);
Which of the following can a Java interface NOT declare?
When is the specific overloaded method to call chosen?
options: At runtime, based on the actual object types of the arguments
When the class is loaded by the JVM
Randomly, if more than one overload matches
At compile time, based on the declared argument types
Compile error: A has no method show() for type B

questions.q: Which statement about abstract classes is true?
options: An abstract class can have constructors
An abstract class can be instantiated directly with new
Every method in an abstract class must be abstract
An abstract class cannot declare fields

questions.q: Which collection type does NOT allow duplicate elements?
What does it mean for a method to be declared static?
options: It can be called only once during the program's lifetime
It belongs to the class and can be called without creating an instance
It can read instance fields directly without an object reference

questions.q: Which statement about a final reference variable is correct?
options: It cannot be reassigned, but the object it refers to can still be modified
The object it refers to automatically becomes immutable
It must always be initialized on the same line it is declared
It cannot be used inside a lambda expression
An ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException is thrown at runtime

title: Java MCQs - Part 2: Advanced
description: Interview-level Java: HashMap internals, the String pool, streams, Optional, records, generics, concurrency and the JVM.

questions.q: Which rule is part of the equals()/hashCode() contract?
options: If a.equals(b) is true, then a.hashCode() must equal b.hashCode()
If a.hashCode() == b.hashCode(), then a.equals(b) must be true
hashCode() must return a unique value for every distinct object
The compiler rejects classes that override equals() without hashCode()

questions.q: In Java 8+ HashMap, what happens when a single bucket accumulates many colliding entries (and the table is large enough)?
options: The bucket is converted into a sorted array
The bucket's linked list is converted into a balanced (red-black) tree
The whole map is converted into a LinkedHashMap
New colliding entries are silently dropped

questions.q:
What is printed?

Stream.of("a", "b", "c")
    .peek(System.out::print)
    .map(String::toUpperCase);
options: Nothing - no terminal operation is invoked, so the pipeline never runs

questions.q: What happens when Optional.of(null) is called?
options: It returns an Optional that contains null

questions.q: Which statement about Java records is true?
options: A record can extend another class
Records generate setter methods for each component
A record is implicitly final and its component fields are private and final

questions.q: Which statement about generics and type erasure is true?
options: You can check obj instanceof List<String> at runtime
Primitive types such as int can be used as type arguments
At runtime, List<String> and List<Integer> share the same Class object
Each parameterization like List<String> gets its own .class file

questions.q: Given List<? extends Number> nums, which call compiles?
Which statement about the volatile keyword is correct?
options: It makes compound operations like count++ atomic
It acquires a monitor lock every time the field is read
It prevents the field from being changed after construction
It guarantees visibility of writes across threads but does not make count++ atomic

questions.q: What happens if you call t.run() instead of t.start() on a Thread object?
options: A new thread is started, exactly as with start()
Nothing happens; run() is a no-op
run() executes synchronously in the calling thread; no new thread is started

questions.q: In Java 8 and later, which JVM memory area holds class metadata?
options: The young generation of the heap

questions.q: When does an object become eligible for garbage collection?
options: When it is no longer reachable from any GC root (live thread stacks, static fields, etc.)
As soon as System.gc() is called
As soon as any one reference to it is set to null
Only after its finalize() method has been called explicitly

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a functional interface?

options: Compile error: static methods cannot be redeclared

title: Python MCQs - Part 1: Fundamentals
description: Test your Python basics: types, slicing, comprehensions, dicts and sets, functions, exceptions and f-strings.

questions.q:
What is the output?

print(type(3 / 2), 7 // 2)
Which built-in type is immutable?

What is the output?

s = "Python"
print(s[1:4], s[-2:])

What is the output?

nums = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
print(nums[::2], nums[::-2])

What is the output?

print([x * x for x in range(5) if x % 2 == 0])
Which expression creates an empty set?

What is the output?

def f(*args, **kwargs):
    print(args, kwargs)

f(1, 2, x=3)

What is the output?

def add(item, bucket=[]):
    bucket.append(item)
    return bucket

add(1)
print(add(2))

What is the output?

a = [1, 2]
b = [1, 2]
print(a == b, a is b)

What happens?

s = "cat"
s[0] = "b"
options: A TypeError is raised because strings are immutable
A new string "bat" is created and bound to s

questions.q: Which of these values is truthy?

What is the output?

price = 3.14159
print(f"{price:.2f}")
Which expression creates a tuple containing exactly one element, the number 5?
What does a Python function return if it finishes without a return statement?

What is the output?

x = 10

def f():
    x = 20

f()
print(x)
What does list.sort() return?
options: A new sorted list, leaving the original unchanged
The original list object after sorting
True if any elements were moved
None - it sorts the list in place

questions.q: Which keyword defines a small anonymous function?

What is the output?

print(list(zip([1, 2, 3], "ab")))
options: A ValueError is raised because the lengths differ

title: Python MCQs - Part 2: Advanced
description: Go deeper into Python: scope and closures, decorators, generators, MRO, dunder methods, context managers and the GIL.

questions.q: In Python's LEGB name-resolution rule, what does LEGB stand for?

What happens when f() is called?

x = 5

def f():
    print(x)
    x = 10

f()

What is the output?

funcs = [lambda: i for i in range(3)]
print([f() for f in funcs])
What is the main purpose of functools.wraps inside a decorator?
options: It caches the wrapped function's results
It lets the decorator accept arguments
It makes the wrapped function thread-safe
It copies metadata such as __name__ and __doc__ from the wrapped function onto the wrapper

questions.q:
What is the output?

def gen():
    yield 1
    yield 2

g = gen()
print(next(g), next(g), next(g, "done"))
What is the main advantage of (x * x for x in data) over [x * x for x in data]?
options: It produces items lazily, so it uses far less memory for large inputs
It can be iterated over any number of times
It is always faster, even for tiny inputs

questions.q: Which two methods make an object an iterator under Python's iterator protocol?

options: A TypeError is raised: inconsistent MRO

questions.q: A class defines __eq__ but not __hash__. What happens when you add an instance to a set?
options: A TypeError is raised because the instance is unhashable
It works, using the default identity-based hash
It works, but the set may contain equal duplicates
An AttributeError is raised because __str__ is missing

questions.q: In a context manager, what happens if __exit__ returns True after an exception occurred inside the with block?
options: The exception is re-raised as usual
The exception is converted into a RuntimeError
The with block is executed again
The exception is suppressed and execution continues after the with block

questions.q: Which statement about the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) in standard CPython 3.11 is true?
options: Only one thread executes Python bytecode at a time, so CPU-bound threads don't run in parallel
It prevents I/O-bound threads from overlapping their waiting time
It makes every operation on shared objects thread-safe, so locks are never needed
It also limits processes created with the multiprocessing module

questions.q: For CPU-bound work in standard CPython, which approach achieves true parallelism across cores?

What is the output?

import copy
a = [[1, 2], [3]]
b = copy.copy(a)
b[0].append(9)
b.append([4])
print(a)
Which statement about dict in Python 3.7+ is true?
options: Keys are always kept in sorted order
Lists can be used as keys
Duplicate keys are stored as separate entries
Insertion order of keys is guaranteed to be preserved
A SyntaxError, because the broader handler comes first

questions.q: What does the if __name__ == "__main__": guard do?
options: Its block runs only when the module is imported
Its block runs only when the file is executed directly, not when it is imported as a module
It marks the module's main function for the compiler
It prevents other modules from importing the file

questions.q:
What is the output?

class Dog:
    tricks = []

a, b = Dog(), Dog()
a.tricks.append("sit")
print(b.tricks)

title: SQL MCQs - Part 1: Fundamentals
description: Check your grip on core SQL: filtering, sorting, joins, grouping, NULL handling, keys and basic DDL.

questions.q: Which clause filters individual rows before any grouping happens?
What is the logical processing order of a SELECT query's clauses?
options: FROM -> WHERE -> GROUP BY -> HAVING -> SELECT -> ORDER BY
SELECT -> FROM -> WHERE -> GROUP BY -> HAVING -> ORDER BY
FROM -> GROUP BY -> WHERE -> HAVING -> SELECT -> ORDER BY
FROM -> WHERE -> SELECT -> GROUP BY -> ORDER BY -> HAVING

questions.q:
Table t has a column x with values 1, NULL, 3, NULL. What does this return?

SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(x) FROM t;
Why does SELECT * FROM t WHERE x = NULL return no rows, even if x has NULLs?
options: NULL rows are always hidden by SELECT *
= NULL is a syntax error in every database
NULLs are stored as empty strings, so they don't match
Comparing with = NULL yields UNKNOWN, never TRUE; you must use IS NULL

questions.q: Column score holds 10, 20 and NULL. What does SELECT AVG(score) return?
What does an INNER JOIN return?
options: Only the rows that have matching values in both tables
All rows from the left table, plus matches from the right
Every combination of rows from both tables
All rows from both tables, matched where possible

questions.q:
customers: Ana, Ben, Cy. orders: two for Ana, one for Ben, none for Cy. How many rows does this return?

SELECT c.name, o.id
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id;
Which statement about a PRIMARY KEY is true?
options: A table can have several separate primary keys
It may contain one NULL value
Its values must be unique and cannot be NULL
It must be an integer column

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a FOREIGN KEY constraint?
options: To speed up every query on the table automatically
To guarantee the column's values are unique
To enforce referential integrity: values must match an existing key in the referenced table

questions.q: If ORDER BY is given without ASC or DESC, how are rows sorted?
Which value matches the condition name LIKE 'J_n%'?

sales(region, amount) has rows ('N',10), ('N',20), ('S',5), ('S',5), ('E',100). What does this return?

SELECT region, SUM(amount)
FROM sales
GROUP BY region
HAVING SUM(amount) > 10
ORDER BY region;
What is the main difference between UNION and UNION ALL?
options: UNION ALL removes duplicates; UNION keeps them
UNION requires the same number of columns; UNION ALL does not
UNION removes duplicate rows from the combined result; UNION ALL keeps them
UNION ALL can only combine two queries

questions.q: Which command removes a table's data AND its structure (definition) from the database?

What does this return when no rows match?

SELECT SUM(x) FROM t WHERE 1 = 0;
Which rows does WHERE age BETWEEN 18 AND 30 include?
options: Ages from 18 to 30, including both 18 and 30

questions.q: A column phone_numbers stores values like '555-1234, 555-9876'. Which normal form does this most directly violate?
Which statement adds a new column to an existing table?
options: ALTER TABLE users ADD email VARCHAR(255);
INSERT INTO users COLUMN email VARCHAR(255);
MODIFY TABLE users NEW email VARCHAR(255);

questions.q: Table a has 4 rows and table b has 3 rows. How many rows does SELECT * FROM a CROSS JOIN b return?
employees(id, name, manager_id) stores each employee's manager as another employee. How do you list each employee with their manager's name?
options: A CROSS JOIN of employees with itself and no condition
A self join: FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.id
GROUP BY manager_id and select name

title: SQL MCQs - Part 2: Advanced
description: Interview-style SQL: window functions, CTEs, subqueries, transactions and isolation levels, indexing and normalization.

questions.q: Scores 100, 90, 90, 80 are ranked with ORDER BY score DESC. What are RANK() and DENSE_RANK() for the score 80?
What is the key difference between an aggregate with GROUP BY and the same aggregate used as a window function (OVER)?
options: Window functions collapse each group into a single row
Window functions cannot use PARTITION BY
Window functions can only be used in the WHERE clause
A window function computes over related rows but keeps every individual row in the result

questions.q:
What does this query return?

WITH RECURSIVE n(x) AS (
  SELECT 1
  UNION ALL
  SELECT x + 1 FROM n WHERE x < 5
)
SELECT SUM(x) FROM n;
When does EXISTS (subquery) evaluate to TRUE?
options: When the subquery returns exactly one row
When every value returned by the subquery is non-NULL
When the subquery's first column equals the outer column
When the subquery returns at least one row

questions.q: What makes a subquery correlated?
options: It appears in the FROM clause
It returns more than one column
It references columns of the outer query, so it is logically evaluated once per outer row
It is joined with a UNION

questions.q: Which ACID property guarantees that a committed transaction survives a crash or power loss?
Per the SQL standard, what is the lowest isolation level that prevents dirty reads?
Per the SQL standard's definitions, which isolation level is the only one that prevents phantom reads?
What is a typical downside of adding many indexes to a table?
options: The table can no longer have a primary key
Rows can no longer contain NULLs
INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE get slower and more storage is used, since every index must be maintained

questions.q: A B-tree index exists on (last_name, first_name). Which WHERE clause can use it most directly, via the leftmost-prefix rule?
In MySQL's InnoDB engine, what is the clustered index of a table that has a primary key?
options: The most recently created secondary index
A hidden index on every column
The primary key - the table rows themselves are stored in primary-key order
There is none; InnoDB never clusters data

questions.q: Which statement about TRUNCATE compared to DELETE is true?
options: TRUNCATE removes all rows at once and cannot take a WHERE clause
TRUNCATE can delete only the rows matching a WHERE condition
TRUNCATE also removes the table's definition
DELETE without a WHERE clause drops the table

questions.q: orders(order_id PK, customer_id, customer_city): customer_city depends on customer_id, not directly on order_id. Which normal form is violated?
options: None; the table is fully normalized

questions.q: Which statement about a standard (non-materialized) view is true?
options: It stores its own copy of the data
It stores a query; its rows are derived from the base tables each time it is queried
Querying it is always faster than querying the base tables
It cannot be used in a JOIN

questions.q:
What effect does the WHERE clause have here?

SELECT c.name
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE o.amount > 100;
options: None; LEFT JOIN always keeps every customer
Customers without orders are removed (o.amount is NULL for them), so it behaves like an INNER JOIN
It returns only customers without orders
It is a syntax error to filter the right table of a LEFT JOIN

questions.q:
Why is this query invalid in standard SQL (and in MySQL with ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY, the default since 5.7)?

SELECT dept, name, COUNT(*)
FROM emp
GROUP BY dept;
options: name is neither in GROUP BY nor inside an aggregate function
COUNT(*) cannot be combined with GROUP BY
GROUP BY must list every table column
dept must appear in an ORDER BY clause

questions.q:
What does this return?

SELECT COALESCE(NULL + 5, 0);

title: REST API MCQs - Part 1: Fundamentals
description: Learn the essentials of REST: HTTP methods, common status codes, resource naming, statelessness and key headers.

questions.q: What does REST stand for?
Which HTTP method is normally used to create a new resource in a collection when the server assigns its ID?

POST /users
Content-Type: application/json

{"name": "Ana"}

The server creates user 17. What is the most appropriate response?
What does the status code 404 Not Found indicate?
options: The server crashed while handling the request
The server can't find a current representation for the requested resource

questions.q: When is 204 No Content typically returned?
options: When the requested resource does not exist
When a request succeeded and there is no response body to send, e.g. after a DELETE
When the client sent an empty request body
When the server is temporarily unavailable

questions.q: Which HTTP method is defined as safe (read-only)?
Which HTTP method is NOT idempotent?
Which endpoint best follows REST resource-naming conventions for listing a user's orders?
What does statelessness mean in REST?
options: Each request carries all the information needed to process it; the server keeps no client session state between requests
The server never stores any data in a database
Clients may not keep any state either

questions.q: A request to a protected endpoint has no credentials (or an invalid token). Which status code fits best?
A logged-in user tries to delete another user's account but lacks permission. Which status code fits best?
What does the Content-Type header in a request indicate?
options: The media types the client accepts in the response
The type of authentication being used
The media type of the request body, e.g. application/json

questions.q: What does the Accept request header do?
options: It tells the server to accept the request without validation
It tells the server which response media types the client can handle (content negotiation)
It lists the HTTP methods the server supports
It carries the client's access token

questions.q: What does 500 Internal Server Error indicate?
options: The server hit an unexpected condition that prevented it from fulfilling the request
The client is not logged in

questions.q: Which is the most RESTful way to request books sorted by price?
options: POST /getProducts with category=books in the body

questions.q: Which statement about REST is true?
options: REST is an architectural style; it doesn't mandate JSON, and a resource can have several representations
REST is a protocol standardized by the W3C
REST APIs must exchange XML documents
REST requires a persistent WebSocket connection

questions.q: What does PUT /users/42 with a complete user representation in the body do?
options: Appends a new user to the /users collection with a server-chosen ID
Updates only the fields that changed and ignores the rest
Replaces the state of the resource at /users/42 with the given representation (or creates it there)
Deletes user 42 and returns its old data

questions.q: A client sends a body containing malformed JSON (a missing closing brace). Which status code fits best?
In a 201 Created response, what does the Location header usually contain?
options: The URI of the newly created resource
The URI of the API documentation

questions.q: Which HTTP method returns the same headers as GET but without a response body?

title: REST API MCQs - Part 2: Advanced
description: Level up on API design: PUT vs PATCH, idempotency, conditional requests and caching, versioning, pagination, CORS and auth.

questions.q: How does PATCH differ from PUT?
options: PATCH creates resources; PUT only deletes them
PATCH is always idempotent; PUT never is
PATCH applies a partial modification; PUT replaces the target resource's entire state
PATCH must send the full resource; PUT sends only changes

questions.q: A client sends DELETE /items/5 twice. The first returns 204, the second 404. Is DELETE still idempotent?
options: No - different status codes prove it is not idempotent
Only if the server returned 204 both times
No - DELETE is defined as non-idempotent
Yes - idempotency concerns the effect on server state, not identical responses

questions.q: A client sends GET /report with If-None-Match: "abc123", and the resource's current ETag is still "abc123". What should the server return?
A client sends PUT /docs/9 with If-Match: "v1", but the document's current ETag is "v2". Which status code should the server return?
Which status code best fits trying to create a user whose username already exists (a conflict with the resource's current state)?
A request contains well-formed JSON, but a field fails a business rule (e.g., age is -5). Which status code is designed for this?
A client exceeds the API's rate limit. Which response is most appropriate?
options: 429 Too Many Requests, optionally with a Retry-After header

questions.q: When is 503 Service Unavailable appropriate?
options: The server is temporarily unable to handle requests, e.g. overload or maintenance
The client used an unsupported HTTP method

questions.q: Per RFC 9110, which header must a 405 Method Not Allowed response include?
Which status code is a permanent redirect that requires the client to keep the original method and body?
What does Cache-Control: no-cache mean?
options: The response must never be stored by any cache
The response may be reused without revalidation for one hour
Caches may store the response but must revalidate it with the origin before each reuse
Only browser caches may store it, never shared caches

questions.q: What is HATEOAS?
options: A token format used to authenticate API calls
A way to compress JSON responses
A protocol for streaming events to clients
Responses include hypermedia links that tell the client which related resources and actions are available

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a common API versioning strategy?
options: A version segment in the URI path, e.g. /v1/orders
A custom header or versioned media type in Accept
Using a different HTTP method for each version

questions.q: What is a key advantage of cursor-based (keyset) pagination over offset-based pagination?
options: Pages stay stable when rows are inserted or deleted, and deep pages stay fast on large datasets
Clients can jump directly to any arbitrary page number
It returns the total row count for free

questions.q: Which statement about CORS is true?
options: Browsers enforce it; the server opts in to cross-origin access with headers such as Access-Control-Allow-Origin
It stops tools like curl or Postman from calling the API
Preflight requests use the HEAD method
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * permits credentialed requests with cookies

questions.q: Which cross-origin browser request triggers a CORS preflight (OPTIONS) request?
options: A GET with no custom headers
A HEAD with no custom headers
A fetch POST with Content-Type: application/json

questions.q: Which statement about a standard signed JWT (JWS) is true?
options: Its payload is encrypted, so it is safe to put passwords in it
The signature prevents the token from being stolen and replayed
Its payload is only Base64URL-encoded, not encrypted, so anyone holding the token can read the claims
A JWT can be revoked instantly just by the client deleting it

questions.q: Which OAuth 2.0 flow is recommended for public clients such as single-page apps and mobile apps?
A payment API lets clients send an Idempotency-Key header with POST /payments. Why?
options: So the server can recognize retries of the same request and avoid creating duplicate charges
To make POST a safe method
To identify which API version to use

questions.q: How is an OAuth 2.0 access token conventionally sent to a resource server?
